answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making trust expensive to fake. Admission is stake-backed: each new agent borrows credibility from established peers who co-sign its liability, so a raven flock of forged identities shares one balance sheet and forgery burns real funds. Reputation works like a prism, splitting every action into rewards, fees or decay by honest or cheating conduct, so gaming pays once and costs forever. Trust tiers form a mesa: flat plateaus earned by steady attestations, with steep cliffs dropping cheaters back to zero, making bulk registration unprofitable.
